summary.text: A 46-year-old man started to experience seizure-like episodes, predominantly at night and lasting tens of minutes. At first they appeared in the early morning hours as bizarre behavior with grunting, blowing, sitting up or rocking movements, and he was mainly unresponsive to verbal stimuli. Frequency rose to 4 to 5 per month and duration to 3 h.

Levetiracetam was introduced with a temporary effect, but increasing doses and eslicarbazepine changed neither frequency nor severity. Blood tests including glucose were normal when measured without symptoms, and interictal EEG showed intermittent slow activity above the left temporal region without epileptiform discharges. Video EEG captured two typical episodes with pre-ictal slowing and significant spectral power changes.

Subsequent routine morning blood tests showed a glucose level of 0.5 mmol/l (9 mg/dL), leading to the correct diagnosis of insulinoma. Thirteen months after the first symptoms the patient underwent surgical removal of the insulinoma; histology confirmed pancreatic insulinoma pT1, N0, M0, G2.

After surgery the patient was seizure-free and antiseizure medication was withdrawn. The patient reports complete relief after removal of the insulinoma and is entirely without nighttime attacks and any antiseizure medication.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Clinical manifestation of insulinoma in our patient – seizures captured during video EEG. (A) Seizure 1 – Video-EEG: The seizure starts with rocking movements (0:12). At 0:32, the patient raises his right hand, throws his legs on the bed, and straightens his shirt sleeve. Rocking motions are repeated (0:54). After the nurse arrives, he says he wants to sleep. He counts aloud at the nurse’s request but only to 2. Then he rocks again, sits up, and grabs the bed rails (1:24). He crosses his arms (2:54) and grunts. At the end of the seizure, he raises his head and hyperventilates (3:32). (B) Seizure 2 – Video-EEG: The seizure again begins with rocking movements. The patient raises his right hand and lifts his legs (0:33). He then kicks his feet from side to side and flexes his right leg (0:43). He rocks again (0:51), sits down, and makes loud noises, tossing his head up and down. He does not recognize the apple and says it is a hat (1:30). At 1:49. He rocks violently, squeals, flails his hands, and stops responding. The seizure ends with arm-stretching (2:10) and tense body posture (2:28).
